expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph: '`ticketdesk` marks each ticket that has passed its due time, so support agents see late work at once...'. File keeps 'Prefix: `TKT`.'. '### Non-goals' with 8 bolded boundaries (no new state, no due-time change, no alerts, no late-close history, no options, no due-soon warning, no change to list order, no color). Also '### Goals'.

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 7 new criteria from the diff: TKT-014, TKT-015, TKT-016, TKT-017, CLI-010, CLI-011, CLI-012. The marker is an amendment paragraph in existing CLI-006, not a new ID. Correct headings, unique, no Testable lines. Bodies 2-4 sentences; TKT-014, TKT-017 and CLI-010 add examples.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: amended CLI-006 'carries the word `OVERDUE` between the state and the title... `#<id> [<priority>] <state> OVERDUE <title>`'. Filter: TKT-017 'returns only the tickets that are overdue'. Order: TKT-017 'due time ascending... ID ascending' + example (5, 7, 2). Exact due: TKT-014 'A ticket whose due time is equal to or later than the time the command runs is not overdue.' + 12:59/13:01 example. Closed: TKT-015 'not overdue, whatever its due time'. Empty: CLI-010 'With no overdue tickets, or with no log file, it prints nothing and exits with code 0.' Stated as a criterion; the empty exit code is also open question 6 in the spec ('Assumption: code 0 with no output') and questions.md Q6.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0).

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: 'Overdue is derived and never recorded... No event records it, and no check for it appends to the log. INV-001, LOG-001, and LOG-009 hold unchanged.' Non-goal: 'No new ticket state.' CLI-010: 'It appends nothing to the log.' INV-002 not cited by ID.

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: TKT-014 'The due time comes from TKT-005.' Non-goal stated outright: 'No change to the order of `list`. TKT-013 holds. Only the line of an overdue ticket changes.' Amended CLI-006 keeps 'in ID order, see TKT-013'.
